newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty firms above three pct from parity.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty firms above three pct from parity.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed above three percent from the trading band centre as inflows exchange bureaux combined with banks' cutting currency exposure ahead of a possible near-term interest rate rise, dealers said.

They said the currency-selling trend was generally weak but strong enough to push the zloty over the psychological barrier of three percent from the parity rate below which it hovered for the last weeks in fear of a central bank intervention.
"Banks, which considered their currency positions too long, probably wanted to cut them ahead of the possible rise in zloty official rates," said Tomasz Wolosz from BRE SA.
Despite the zloty's rise the central bank did not intervenue on the market. The zloty closed up at 3.08/3.01 percent from parity, up from yesterday's 2.96/2.93 percent.
It closed at 2.8530/50 to the dollar, up from 2.8615/27 on Monday and at 1.8430/45 to the mark, down from 1.8403/09.
A newspaper report said on Tuesday the central bank would consider a rate rise if credit continued to grow as fast as in recent months.
Lending to households rose 89.6 percent in January-November period, while personal deposits grew by 38.9 percent.
